description: Household planner epic, decomposed from the 2026-09-01 review of the recipe, grocery and meal-planner modules across web and the Swift iOS app. The Expo client under app/ is retired (decision 2026-09-01, removed by US-720); Android is the Kotlin app under android-native/ and is out of scope for this epic. Goal: one kitchen loop (recipe in, week planned, list generated, shop, stock, cook) that works for every eater in the house, not only children with a pickiness profile. Slices: 1 fix-now bugs and security, 2 one entry primitive plus grocery categorization and structured recipes, 3 kitchen-loop slice 3 dependencies plus household eaters, 4 planner and grocery features people ask for, 5 iOS parity. Stories that depend on prd-kitchen-loop.json say so in notes and must not duplicate that work. loopVerifiable follows the kitchen-loop convention: true when vitest, the typecheck and lint ratchets, or a disposable Postgres can prove it from this machine; false for edge functions that need a deployed target and for Swift.

userStories.title: Remove the client-supplied AI model path from parse-recipe
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I want parse-recipe to resolve its own model so that no signed-in user can name a server env var and an endpoint and receive the secret.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/parse-recipe/index.ts no longer reads aiModel from the request body; the branch that calls Deno.env.get(aiModel.api_key_env_var) and fetches aiModel.endpoint_url is deleted
src/components/ImportRecipeDialog.tsx no longer selects from ai_settings; the request carries only url, text or imageBase64
A request that still sends aiModel is ignored, not honoured; a test asserts the function returns 200 using AIServiceV2 with aiModel present in the body
supabase/config.toml keeps verify_jwt for parse-recipe consistent with the other user-facing functions and requireUser remains in place
grep across supabase/functions for api_key_env_var finds only _shared/ai-service-v2.ts reading its own server-side settings row
userStories.notes: Review item 1. Verified in source at parse-recipe/index.ts:84-112 and ImportRecipeDialog.tsx:191-205. Ship before anything else in this epic. Landed 2026-09-01: the aiModel branch is gone from parse-recipe and from suggest-recipe, which carried the identical hole and now also runs requireUser; both resolve their model through AIServiceV2. parse-recipe moved to verify_jwt = true, matching suggest-recipe and suggest-recipes-from-pantry. AC 5 narrowed: test-ai-model, suggest-recipes-from-pantry and repurpose-content still read api_key_env_var, but off an ai_settings row they fetch themselves with the service-role client, never off caller input; test-ai-model exists to validate exactly that row. Migrating those three to AIServiceV2 is a separate change. The allowlist is pinned in src/lib/clientAiConfig.guard.test.ts so a fourth cannot be added silently. AC 3's runtime 200 assertion is a static source guard instead: deno is not installed on the loop machine and CI runs only two named deno test files, so a mocked handler test would never execute. The guard was verified to fail when the branch is reintroduced.

userStories.title: SSRF, timeout and size guards on recipe URL fetch
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I want URL import to refuse internal addresses and unbounded bodies so that the parser cannot be used to read the metadata service or local services.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared fetchRecipePage helper in supabase/functions/_shared rejects any scheme other than https, resolves the host and rejects RFC1918, loopback, link-local and 169.254.169.254 before fetching
Redirects are followed manually with a cap of 3 and every hop is re-validated
AbortSignal.timeout(10000) on the fetch; the body is read with a 2 MB cap and a 413 is returned above it
parse-recipe and parse-recipe-grocery both call the helper; the direct fetch(url, {redirect:'follow'}) calls are gone
Unit tests under supabase/functions/_shared cover the private-range rejection, the redirect cap and the size cap
userStories.notes: Review item 2. parse-recipe-grocery/index.ts:68 and parse-recipe/index.ts:58. Landed 2026-09-01: supabase/functions/_shared/url-validator.ts exports fetchRecipePage (https-only, credentials rejected, private/loopback/link-local and 169.254.169.254 refused before the fetch, DNS-resolved hosts re-checked, redirect:'manual' with a cap of 3 and every hop re-validated, AbortSignal.timeout(10000) per hop, 2 MB body cap -> 413). parse-recipe and parse-recipe-grocery both call it; both redirect:'follow' calls are gone. 16 Deno tests in supabase/functions/_shared/url-validator.test.ts inject fetchImpl and use IP literals, so they need no network and no --allow-net; ci.yml runs them as a named step beside the other two Deno tests. Ported from the non-deployed functions/_shared/url-validator.ts, which had this all along -- the deployed tree never got it. loopVerifiable should be true for this one: deno installs as a single binary and the tests are hermetic.

userStories.title: Household-scope RLS on recipe_ingredients and recipe_components
userStories.description: As a household member, I want to see the ingredients of a recipe my partner saved so that the recipe is usable by everyone who can already see it.
acceptanceCriteria: New additive migration replaces every policy on public.recipe_ingredients and public.recipe_components whose predicate is r.user_id = auth.uid() with r.household_id = public.get_user_household_id(auth.uid())
SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE are all household-scoped, matching the recipes policies from 20251008035900
Applied to a disposable postgres:16 container with the auth.uid() stub used by the kitchen-loop migrations; a second household member can select the rows, a user from another household cannot
No column, table or policy name is dropped that a shipped iOS build references
userStories.notes: Review item 3. Verified: 20260430000001_create_recipe_ingredients.sql:44-52 and 20260806000000_recipe_components.sql:105 still owner-scoped; no later migration touches these policies. Landed 2026-09-01: 20260901000009_household_scope_recipe_children.sql replaces the predicate on all eight policies with r.household_id = public.get_user_household_id(auth.uid()), keeping the eight policy names byte-identical so nothing that looks them up by name breaks. Verified on a real PostgreSQL 16.13 (a local cluster, not a container -- this machine has psql and postgres 16 but no docker daemon) with the auth.uid() stub reading request.jwt.claim.sub: owner still 1/1, partner 0/0 -> 1/1, outsider 0/0 and still refused on INSERT, partner can now INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Re-applying the migration is a clean no-op. Fixture and assertions shipped as supabase/tests/us711_recipe_children_household_rls.{bootstrap,test}.sql.

userStories.title: Stop deleting checked grocery items on page mount
userStories.description: As a shopper, I want the items I checked off to survive a page reload so that an interrupted trip does not lose what I already bought.
acceptanceCriteria: The mount effect in src/pages/Grocery.tsx that calls deleteGroceryItems on every checked row is removed along with its toast
Checked rows remain visible in a collapsed Purchased section until the user takes the explicit checkout action
The checkout action is the only path that removes purchased rows, and it credits the pantry (movements when the ledger flag is on, foods.quantity otherwise) before removing them
A test in src/pages renders Grocery with pre-checked items from the cache and asserts no delete call is made on mount
userStories.notes: Review item 4. Verified at Grocery.tsx:155-167. Landed 2026-09-01: the mount effect, its toast, the hasAutoCleanedRef guard and the now-unused deleteGroceryItems destructure are all gone from Grocery.tsx. AC 2 and AC 3 already held before this change and were re-verified rather than built: the collapsed Purchased Collapsible is at Grocery.tsx:1140 and handleDoneShopping credits via recordPurchases when ledgerWritesEnabled and via updateFood/addFood otherwise, then calls clearCheckedGroceryItems. The only other removal path is handleDeleteItem, an explicit per-row delete with an Undo toast. src/pages/Grocery.mountCleanup.test.tsx renders the real page with a pre-checked row from the store; 3 of its 4 assertions fail when the effect is put back, which was checked. Typecheck: adds zero errors (HEAD without it and the working tree with it both measure exactly 1400), but the ratchet fails on both because the committed baseline of 1165 is 235 below a real full run -- a pre-existing condition tracked as an open finding in progress.txt, not caused by this story.

userStories.title: Sync from meal plan persists through the merge path
userStories.description: As a parent, I want the grocery list I generate from the plan to exist on the server so that it survives a reload and reaches my partner's phone.
acceptanceCriteria: handleRegenerateFromPlan in src/pages/Grocery.tsx no longer calls setGroceryItems; new rows go through addGroceryItemsMerged and retired auto-generated rows through deleteGroceryItems
generateGroceryList in src/lib/mealPlanner.ts takes a from/to date range and the caller passes the shopping window, defaulting to the visible week, instead of the whole 120-day context window
Generated rows carry grocery_list_id of the selected list and source_plan_entry_id of the entry that caused them
Re-running generation for the same week does not create duplicate rows; a vitest covers idempotence
The is_manual filter is replaced by the persisted auto_generated column so hand-added rows are genuinely preserved
userStories.notes: Review item 5 and grocery items G12, G18. Verified: GroceryContext.setGroceryItems is local state only. Full recipe-aware quantities land in US-736; this story makes the path persist and idempotent. Landed 2026-09-02: handleRegenerateFromPlan no longer calls setGroceryItems. New rows go through addGroceryItemsMerged stamped with grocery_list_id, auto_generated and source_plan_entry_id (GroceryAddInput and the insert row in GroceryContext gained all three); rows the plan no longer calls for go through deleteGroceryItems. generateGroceryList takes an optional ShoppingWindow and the page passes the current Mon-Sun week. One deviation worth knowing: auto_generated alone cannot decide what a sync may retire, because auto_add_restock_items (20251010221000) sets the same flag -- its column comment still reads 'added by restock system'. Retiring on that flag alone would delete the user's restock suggestions on every sync, so a row is regenerable only when it also carries source_plan_entry_id or added_via = 'meal_plan_sync'. That preserves strictly more than the AC asks. The is_manual swap also reached the checkout-undo payloads, which carried is_manual and so restored a plan row as a hand-added one that no sync would ever retire. 17 vitest in src/lib/planSync.test.ts, idempotence covered both on the planner alone and end to end through generateGroceryList. Typecheck: 1398 errors against 1400 on origin/main -- this removes the two is_manual errors and adds none, verified by diffing the error sets.

userStories.title: Every grocery add path lands on the selected list
userStories.description: As a shopper, I want an item I add to appear on the list I am looking at so that the add button is trusted.
acceptanceCriteria: AddGroceryItemDialog receives selectedListId and includes grocery_list_id in onAdd; Grocery.tsx passes it

addGroceryItem, addGroceryItemsMerged, restock suggestions, receipt scan and recipe import all carry grocery_list_id; the merge insert in GroceryContext also carries brand_preference, barcode, priority, price_per_unit and added_by_user_id
filterItemsByList in src/lib/groceryData.ts treats grocery_list_id null as belonging to the household's default list
planGroceryMerge merges only against rows on the target list; a vitest asserts that adding milk to list B does not bump list A
userStories.notes: Review items 6, G14, G18. Verified at AddGroceryItemDialog.tsx:164-175 and groceryData.ts:47. Landed 2026-09-02: AddGroceryItemDialog takes selectedListId and stamps grocery_list_id on both its onAdd call sites (manual and the import tab); Grocery.tsx passes it. Restock suggestions, the checkout-undo payload and the plan sync now stamp it too; recipe import and delete-undo already did. filterItemsByList takes defaultListId and treats a null grocery_list_id as belonging to it, with GroceryListSelector reporting which list is default via a new onDefaultListChange (it already fetched the lists; nothing else knew). planGroceryMerge takes a scope and indexes only rows on the target list. ScanReceiptDialog is NOT covered: it adds to the pantry, not to a grocery list, so there is nothing to stamp -- AC 2's 'receipt scan' has no grocery add path today. The merge insert also stopped being a hand-written column allowlist: it spreads the input, which is what carries brand_preference, barcode, priority, price_per_unit and added_by_user_id, and which also repaired US-713 (see progress.txt). 10 vitest in src/lib/listScoping.test.ts. Typecheck 1397 vs origin/main's 1400: three removed (both is_manual errors plus a restock priority mismatch fixed by narrowing SmartRestockSuggestions' onAddItems priority to the real union), zero added.

A single N items need confirming affordance on Grocery and Pantry lists provisional items; proposeMerges from itemMergeProposals is surfaced there as a reviewable merge (US-664 owns the merge UI, this story links to it)
Tests cover confident, provisional and confirmed paths on the grocery add
userStories.notes: Review items G5, G17, G25 (identity part). Complements kitchen-loop US-661 (recipes) and US-664 (merge UI); do not duplicate those.

userStories.title: Seed canonical_products
userStories.description: As a new household, I want common products already known so that resolution does not start from zero.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/seed/canonical-products.mjs builds a CSV from Open Food Facts and USDA FoodData Central subsets with normalized_name run through normalizeItemText, category, default_unit, default_aisle and barcode when present; sources and licences recorded in the script header
A migration or a documented supabase db seed step loads at least 3000 rows; the migration is additive and re-runnable (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on barcode and normalized_name)
A test fixture asserts that resolveItem finds ground beef, whole milk and honeycrisp apples through step 4 with an empty alias table
The open question in the kitchen-loop spec about seeding is answered in the spec
userStories.notes: Review items G6, G13 (normalized_name must be pre-normalized).

userStories.title: Store walk order on the web list
userStories.description: As a shopper, I want the list grouped in the order I walk the store so that I do not backtrack.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/storeWalkOrder.ts ports walkOrder(for:layoutId:) from Swift, reading store_layouts.aisle_overrides and user_store_layout_overrides
A list can pick its store (grocery_lists.store_layout_id is set by CreateGroceryListDialog and ManageGroceryListsDialog); selectedStoreLayoutId in Grocery.tsx is driven by the selected list
Groups in Grocery.tsx are sorted by walk order; insertion-order grouping is gone
store_aisles from ManageStoreAislesDialog is honoured as a per-store override
Fixture-based test for the five seeded layouts
userStories.notes: Review item G8. Seeds exist in 20260507000000_store_layouts.sql with no JS reader.

userStories.title: Parse schema.org recipes directly and keep the image
userStories.description: As a cook importing from a site, I want exact ingredients, times and the photo so that import is fast and faithful.
acceptanceCriteria: One parse function (parse-recipe-grocery retired or merged) parses HTML with deno-dom, walks @graph recursively, decodes entities, and reads recipeIngredient, recipeInstructions including HowToSection and HowToStep, recipeYield, prepTime, cookTime, totalTime, nutrition, aggregateRating and image directly when a Recipe schema exists
The model is called only when no schema is found, and its output is validated with the same zod schema; the fabricated Imported Recipe fallback returns 422 with the raw text instead
Ingredient strings are parsed server-side into quantity, unit, name and prep using the shared line parser (parseGroceryText fixtures), returning objects in one snake_case shape
The recipe image is fetched, stored in the images bucket under the household path and its URL returned; the source URL is stored for attribution; og:image is the fallback
Photo import stores the captured image and sets source_type photo; the TS source_type union matches the CHECK
ImportRecipeDialog opens EnhancedRecipeBuilder prefilled for review instead of saving immediately, and warns when source_url already exists in the household
userStories.notes: Review items R1, R2, R3, R4, R6, R7, R8, R9, R17. R5 (resolver at import) is kitchen-loop US-661, which adds the confirm step inside this same review sheet; not duplicated here.

userStories.title: Remove dead recipe surfaces and fix the AI buttons that cannot succeed
userStories.description: As a user, I want every recipe button to work or not exist.
acceptanceCriteria: RecipeImporter.tsx and RecipeBuilder.tsx are deleted after grep confirms no importer
Generate with AI in EnhancedRecipeBuilder sends selectedFoodNames matching suggest-recipe, or the button is removed
suggest-recipes-from-pantry calls AIServiceV2.generateContent({messages}, taskType) and the unused ai_settings fetch is removed; saved suggestions carry recipe_ingredients rows with quantities
RecipeExportActions is mounted in RecipeDetailView (print, copy ingredients, email)
RecipeShareButton is removed until a public share route exists (US-748)
A paste-from-clipboard button and URL auto-detect are added to the import dialog
userStories.notes: Review items R10, R11, R23 (export part).

userStories.title: Core-loop analytics events and one loop integration test
userStories.description: As the product owner, I want the seven loop steps measured so that decisions stop favouring the only features that are instrumented.
acceptanceCriteria: trackEvent calls for meal_planned, grocery_generated, grocery_item_checked, shop_completed, pantry_stocked, meal_cooked and recipe_created with household_id, platform and source properties, emitted once per action (not per rendered card)
The per-card telemetry effects in DraggableMealItem are removed
src/test/kitchenLoop.integration.test.tsx walks recipe create, plan, generate list, check off, checkout and cook against the mocked Supabase client and asserts each event fired once
Analytics contract documented in docs/analytics-events.md with the Swift AnalyticsContractTests names aligned
userStories.notes: Review items X4, P19 (telemetry). Do this in slice 1; it is half a day and reframes everything after.

userStories.title: Recipe-aware grocery generation with servings and pantry subtraction
userStories.description: As a parent, I want the list to reflect what the planned recipes need for the people eating, minus what we have, so that I buy the right amounts.
acceptanceCriteria: generateGroceryList expands each plan entry with a recipe into its recipe_ingredients scaled by servings_planned over recipe base servings, in canonical units via canonicalUnits.toCanonical; unknown conversions are listed in the item's own unit and flagged, never fudged
Requirements are grouped by item id (falling back to ingredientMatchKey only for unresolved rows), then requiredAfterStock subtracts item_stock when the ledger flag is on and foods.quantity otherwise
Package rounding uses foods.package_quantity when present
recipeShortfall.computeRecipeShortfall converts units through unitNormalize.convert; the string-equality comparable check is deleted so the planner badge and the grocery dialog agree
Property-style vitest: for random plans the generated list plus stock covers the requirement
userStories.notes: Review items G12, G24, P24, R29. This is kitchen-loop US-676 and US-680 from the grocery side; coordinate so one shortfall function exists, not two.

userStories.title: Grocery list as a projection of the plan
userStories.description: As a parent, I want adding, swapping or removing a meal to update the list by itself so that the list is never stale.
acceptanceCriteria: On every planMeal call and every meal update or delete, the shortfall for that meal is recomputed and written to grocery_item_sources(meal or plan_entry ref, grocery_item_id, required quantity); grocery_items.quantity is the sum over its sources plus any manual delta
Removing or swapping a meal removes its source rows and decrements or deletes the grocery row; a manual row is never deleted by this path
source_plan_entry_id (and meal_id once US-674 lands) is written on generated rows; regenerate becomes recompute-all-sources for the window
A per-add Add missing to grocery toggle on the web quick-add drawer (the pattern the Expo planner had) and MissingIngredientsDialog both call the same projection function
A By Meal view on Grocery lists rows grouped by the meal that needs them; tapping a row shows for Tuesday stir-fry you have 200 g of 500 g
Tests: add then remove a meal leaves the list unchanged; two meals sharing an item produce one row with the summed quantity
userStories.notes: Review items P23, R30. grocery_item_sources exists since 20260430000002 with zero readers or writers.

userStories.title: Cooked action on web through rpc_mark_meal_made_v2
userStories.description: As a cook, I want marking a meal cooked to take the ingredients out of the pantry and tick the sourced grocery rows so that stock stays honest without a chore.
acceptanceCriteria: A Cooked action on the planner cell, Today card and Tonight Mode calls rpc_mark_meal_made_v2 with quantities scaled to servings; the deduct_food_quantity {_amount: 1} calls are removed
With the ledger flag on, the RPC (or a v3) appends one cook movement per resolved ingredient with ref_type meal; undo appends reversals via rpc_undo_meal_made
Cooking does not write plan_entries.result; per-plate outcomes are logged separately (kitchen-loop US-679)
Grocery rows sourced from the meal are auto-checked
Tonight Mode Cook now creates today's dinner meal through planMeal, marks it cooked, then opens the cook dialog; its grocery add uses the merge path with inferred category and real quantities
Tests cover scaled debit, auto-check and undo
userStories.notes: Review items G23, P25, P29. Sequenced after kitchen-loop US-674 (meals) and US-677 (rpc_cook_meal); if those slip, implement against plan_entries and migrate.

userStories.title: Checkout credits the pantry by item id, once, with undo
userStories.description: As a shopper, I want Done shopping to stock the pantry correctly so that I never see duplicate pantry rows or double counts.
acceptanceCriteria: A single checkout action on web writes one purchase movement per checked row using grocery_items.item_id (resolved at add time by US-730); the five lowercased-name matches in Grocery.tsx are removed
The wasSkipped double-credit branch is removed; a row that resolves by item id never also creates a new food
Undo reads current state at click time and appends reversal movements; it does not close over a stale foods array
Price entered at checkout or from a receipt is stored on the movement and on the item as last-known price

The mobile-width web grocery view gains a shopping mode with keep-awake (Screen Wake Lock API, re-acquired on visibilitychange), swipe-to-check and a non-destructive primary gesture, matching Swift ShoppingModeView
Before the ledger flag defaults on, the stockComparison dark-launch telemetry is confirmed to be collected on real households and the agreement rate is recorded in notes
Tests cover credit-once, undo and the price path
userStories.notes: Review items G25, G26, G27 (checkout part), G28, G15 (capture part). Kitchen-loop US-672 owns the movement writers; this story wires the UI to them.

userStories.title: Household eaters: adults plan too
userStories.description: As an adult, I want to plan meals for myself and my partner so that EatPal is a household planner, not only a kids tool.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration adds public.household_eaters(id, household_id, kind check in ('adult','child'), display_name, kid_id null references kids, member_user_id null, dietary_restrictions text[], allergens text[], is_active) with RLS; every existing kid is backfilled as a child eater
Migration adds public.meal_attendees(meal_id, eater_id) with RLS, and makes plan_entries.kid_id nullable once plan_entries.meal_id exists (kitchen-loop US-674); no column is dropped
Onboarding opens with Who are you planning for: just me, me and a partner, my family; only the family branch asks for a child, and the planner renders for a household with zero kids
ManageHouseholdDialog lists eaters and lets an adult member mark themselves as an eater with restrictions
Planner family mode renders one grid with a row per eater rather than one planner instance per kid; nutrition is loaded once through a cached query
The Swift MealPlanView empty state and OnboardingView copy are updated in the same release so the two funnels do not diverge
Reminders derive household from plan_entries.household_id, not from kids
userStories.notes: Review items P2, P14, X5 (onboarding part), P32 (kids join). Verified: plan_entries.kid_id NOT NULL, Planner.tsx:574 blocks without kids, OnboardingDialog.tsx:182 requires a child name.

userStories.title: Gate kid tooling and unify navigation
userStories.description: As a household without a picky eater, I want the primary navigation to be the kitchen loop so that clinical tools do not crowd it.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/nav.ts exports one NAV array consumed by AppSidebar, Navigation, CommandPalette and QuickActionsMenu; the four hand-maintained lists are removed
Food Chaining, Food Tracker, Progress, Sibling Meal Finder and the Kids selector appear only when at least one child eater has a pickiness profile; a household can opt in from settings
Primary sections are Today, Week, Recipes, Grocery (with a Pantry segment) and Kids, matching the kitchen-loop iOS layout
The signed-in document titles no longer read ARFID and Picky Eater Meal Planner; marketing pages keep their positioning
QuickActionsMenu leads with Plan a meal and Add to list, not Add Child
userStories.notes: Review items X5, X13 (naming). Web IA rework was out of scope in the kitchen-loop spec; this story brings it in once eaters exist.

userStories.title: Servings, recurrence, leftovers and eating out on a meal
userStories.description: As a parent, I want Taco Tuesday every week, Friday takeout and Wednesday leftovers to be plannable so that the list stops buying for meals we will not cook.
acceptanceCriteria: meals gains kind text check in ('cook','leftover_of','eating_out','packed') default 'cook' and source_meal_id uuid null; leftover_of and eating_out contribute nothing to the grocery projection and leftover_of debits nothing on cook
recipes.servings is stored numerically (servings_default already exists) and the detail view scales ingredient rows and nutrition from it

New table public.meal_recurrences(household_id, slot, weekday, recipe_id or title, eaters, starts_on, ends_on) with RLS, expanded lazily into meals when a week is opened; editing one occurrence detaches it
Planner cells show a kind badge; the quick-add sheet offers Leftovers of and Eating out
Tests cover expansion, detach and the projection exclusions
userStories.notes: Review items P3, P4, R13. Depends on kitchen-loop US-674.

userStories.title: Range, month and agenda views; copy from any week
userStories.description: As a planner, I want to see two weeks or a month and copy last week into this one so that the grid fits how I plan.
acceptanceCriteria: The planner grid takes a days parameter (1, 3, 7, 14, 28) with a view switcher; a month view shows one line per meal and an agenda view lists meals chronologically
Copy week is a source-to-target picker with merge or replace, so last week can be copied forward and a template week can be copied from any past week
The plan window fetch in AppContext gets an explicit limit and fetches the visible range on navigation instead of relying on the PostgREST max-rows cap
Planner reads ?date= and ?slot= from the URL and scrolls to them, so reminders and shared links land on the right day
Tests cover the range switch and the copy picker
userStories.notes: Review items P11, X12, P32 (deep link part).

userStories.title: Keyboard-accessible, reliable drag and drop
userStories.description: As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want to move a meal without a pointer, and as any user I want a drop to land where I let go.
acceptanceCriteria: The move commits on drag end before the animation, using elementFromPoint hit-testing instead of nearest-centroid; unmounting mid-tween cannot drop a move
Cells have role gridcell inside role grid, are focusable, and Space or Enter picks up a meal, arrow keys choose a target, Enter drops, Escape cancels; an aria-live region announces the result

Moving or twisting operates on the meal (all its plates) in family mode and only the active eater's plate in single mode; Twist re-schedules through planMeal so ingredients and shortfall follow the new recipe
Variety-fatigue memos key on a content hash of (recipe_id, date) pairs, not array length
Playwright a11y test covers the keyboard move
userStories.notes: Review items P12, P13, P19.

userStories.title: Household-level plan generation
userStories.description: As a household, I want the generator to plan for everyone with our constraints so that Quick Build and AI Week are useful beyond a single picky eater.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/ai-meal-plan accepts {householdId, range, eaterIds, constraints: {maxPrepMinutesByWeekday, weeklyBudget, dietaryRestrictions, batchCook, leftoverPolicy}} and reads pantry, recipes and history server-side; the client no longer ships foods and recipes in the request
The function returns {recipe_id | food_id | title} per slot; unmatched names are returned as titles for the user to confirm, never dropped; ARFID rules for child eaters are applied as constraints
buildWeekPlan becomes a deterministic seeded scorer over varietyFatigue, pantry coverage (depletion forecast) and ladder due-ness from ladderScheduler; Math.random selection is removed
Household settings gain per-weekday max prep minutes and a weekly budget; the planner shows an over budget chip on a day
Generated weeks are written through planMeal (US-724) and are reviewable before commit
Tests cover the scorer's determinism and the constraint filters
userStories.notes: Review items P27, P28, P31 (schedule awareness). Edge-function half is loopVerifiable false; the scorer is pure TS.

userStories.title: Pantry coverage and depletion forecast in the planner
userStories.description: As a parent, I want the week to tell me I will run out of milk before Thursday's pancakes so that shopping happens before the problem.
acceptanceCriteria: Each meal cell shows a coverage badge (covered, short N items, unknown) from the single shortfall function, matching the iOS PantryCoverage badge
forecastForFood from depletionForecast.ts is evaluated per planned ingredient against the meal's date and surfaces a will run out by chip on the day
platePlanner KidPlate breakdowns render inside the dinner cell when the meal has child eaters with restrictions
Coverage is computed once per week load, not per cell render
Tests cover the badge states
userStories.notes: Review items P26, P30 (plates), R20.

userStories.title: Reminders that fire, in the right timezone, once per meal, plus partner notifications
userStories.description: As a household, I want dinner and shopping reminders that arrive at the right time and tell me what my partner planned so that the plan is a shared thing.
acceptanceCriteria: A pg_cron entry (following 20260818000001_trial_reminder_emails.sql) invokes schedule-meal-reminders on a schedule; profiles.timezone is added and used to compute local instants
One notification per meal per household member, not per plate; deep link carries date and slot

New notification types: dinner_tonight at a user-chosen hour naming the planned meal, partner_planned_meal and partner_checked_items (rate limited to one digest per hour), pantry_expiring on web, shopping_day nudge when the projected list is non-empty
The four weekly-report functions are consolidated into one with a documented schedule
userStories.notes: Review items P32, X14 (reports). Verified: nothing schedules schedule-meal-reminders today.

userStories.title: ICS feed and read-only week share
userStories.description: As a co-parent or nanny without an account, I want to see this week's plan in my calendar so that the plan leaves the app.
acceptanceCriteria: New table public.household_share_tokens(household_id, token, scope check in ('plan_ics','week_view','recipe'), expires_at, revoked_at) with RLS on management and no anon read; edge function plan-ics validates the token with the service role and emits one VEVENT per meal with slot default times
Settings shows the feed URL with copy and revoke
A prerendered public route /share/week/:token renders the week read-only with no PII beyond meal names; /share/recipe/:token renders a recipe and replaces the broken RecipeShareButton URL
Tests cover token expiry and the VEVENT output
userStories.notes: Review items P32 (ICS), R23.

userStories.title: Price capture, trip total and per-store price history
userStories.description: As the household budget holder, I want to know what we actually spend and where it is cheaper so that the grocery app pays for itself.
acceptanceCriteria: receiptParse keeps unitPrice and lineTotal; the receipt review sheet writes them to purchase movements and to the item's last-known price
Checkout allows an optional price per row; the shopping view shows a running estimated total from last-known prices and an actual total after checkout
New view or table item_price_history(item_id, store_layout_id, price, currency, observed_at) fed from movements; the item detail shows cheaper at X when two stores differ
BudgetService-equivalent on web reports actual spend by week from movements instead of estimates
Tests cover the movement price path and the history rollup
userStories.notes: Review item G15. Columns exist since 20260426000000; buildPurchaseMovement already accepts price.

userStories.title: Ranked recipe search, cookable-now query, cook history and per-person ratings
userStories.description: As a cook, I want to find a recipe by an ingredient, see what I can make right now from my own library, and know when we last made it and who liked it.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration adds a generated tsvector over recipes name, tags and recipe_ingredients names with a GIN index, an index on recipes(household_id, created_at desc), cuisine and course columns with fixed vocabularies, and diet_flags text[]
One shared searchRecipes in src/lib used by web: server tsquery plus client Damerau-Levenshtein re-rank; web search covers ingredients and instructions

New table recipe_cook_events(recipe_id, meal_id, cooked_on, servings_made, cooked_by, notes) written by the Cooked action; the detail view shows made N times, last made, and per-eater outcomes from meal_votes and plan outcomes
recipe_ratings(recipe_id, eater_id, rating) replaces the single scalar; the scalar becomes a rollup for shipped clients
Recipe library loads with cursor pagination; collections are loaded once in context and memberships filtered by collection
Tests cover ranking, the cookable query and the rating rollup
userStories.notes: Review items R14, R16, R19, R20, R21, R24, R25.

userStories.title: Recipe detail and cook mode fixes
userStories.description: As a cook, I want the detail view to show amounts, scale correctly, and keep the screen on in the kitchen.
acceptanceCriteria: RecipeDetailView renders 2 cups flour from recipe_ingredients, scales rows and nutrition by the serving control, and shows pantry stock as a secondary badge
Hooks are called before the early return; new URL(source_url) is guarded
Nutrition is computed from quantities through canonicalUnits against per-100g data and shows unknown when a conversion is missing; the one-of-each sum is removed
CookMode gains a pinned ingredient drawer, per-step timers, and re-acquires the wake lock on visibilitychange
The household recipe library snapshot is available offline for reads via the service worker
A recipe_ingredients realtime subscription by household folds ingredient edits into the loaded recipe
userStories.notes: Review items R12, R13, R18, R22, R26, R27.

userStories.title: Grocery list mechanics: deltas, quantities, presence, export
userStories.description: As a household shopping together, I want concurrent edits to add up, fractional quantities to work, and to see who is shopping.
acceptanceCriteria: bump_grocery_item_quantities takes deltas and sets quantity = quantity + delta; the realtime reducer ignores an echo whose updated_at is older than local state
One QuantityInput component with unit-aware steps (0.25 for weight and volume, 1 for count) replaces the stepper that floors at 1 and the dialog that allows 0.25
priority and added_by_user_id are persisted and rendered (sort by priority, avatar of who added)
CollaborativeShoppingMode is wired to the household channel as presence (who is shopping, who ticked this) or deleted
The two per-check-off queries are replaced by one preload per list; Smart Restock refetch is household-filtered and limited; restock rows carry the item's unit, never servings
CSV export escapes quotes; grocery toggles queue in the service worker when offline
Tests cover delta merge, the quantity component and presence
userStories.notes: Review items G13, G16, G17, G18, G19, G20, G21, G22.

userStories.title: One add-item sheet with input modes
userStories.description: As a user, I want one way to add something anywhere that offers type, voice, scan, photo and paste so that every add behaves the same.
acceptanceCriteria: src/components/AddItemSheet.tsx with mode tabs type, paste, scan, photo; it owns parsing (parseGroceryText, pantryQuickAddParser), resolution (US-730), unit suggestion and category inference, and takes a target (grocery list, pantry, recipe ingredients, plan slot)
AddFoodDialog, BulkAddFoodDialog, AddGroceryItemDialog, FoodSelectorDialog, ImportRecipeToGroceryDialog, MissingIngredientsDialog and PantryQuickAdd are replaced by it or become thin wrappers
EmptyState.tsx is used for the empty grocery, pantry, planner and recipes states
Tests cover each mode's parse path against the shared fixtures
userStories.notes: Review items X7 and the EmptyState note from the cohesion review. The unit-suggestions data lands in US-728.

userStories.title: Platform map and a findable minimum iOS build
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want the platform map and the minimum supported iOS build documented so that CLAUDE.md's migration rule can actually be checked.
acceptanceCriteria: PLATFORMS.md (created by US-720) lists, per client, which loop steps it implements today and which stories in this epic and prd-kitchen-loop.json bring it to parity
ios/README.md no longer says Sentry is not wired on iOS; it points at SentryService.swift

CLAUDE.md states that the minimum supported iOS build lives in app_config.min_ios_build, read by ios/EatPal/EatPal/Services/ForceUpdateService.swift, and gives the read-only query to fetch it; the Migration Rules section links to it
npm run ios:min-build prints the value when a read-only target is configured and exits 0 with no target configured, following scripts/ci/schema-drift-report.mjs (no credential in the script)
userStories.notes: Review items X1 (docs part), X14 (min build). The Expo removal itself is US-720.

userStories.title: Make npm run typecheck check src and put budgets on the ratchets
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the local typecheck to reach src so that a green run means something.
acceptanceCriteria: tsconfig.node.json declares types node and resolves vite, @vitejs/plugin-react-swc, lovable-tagger and @sentry/vite-plugin; tsc -b no longer aborts on vite.config.ts
rm -f *.tsbuildinfo && npm run typecheck reports the same error count as scripts/ci/typecheck-ratchet.sh
PlanEntry, GroceryItem and Recipe UI types are derived from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts; the three @ts-expect-error in PlanContext.copyWeekPlan are removed
.ci/typecheck-baseline.txt and .ci/lint-baseline.txt each drop by at least 100 in this story, and a monthly reduction target is written into CLAUDE.md
userStories.notes: Review items X11, P6 (type part).

userStories.title: One design token source for web and Swift
userStories.description: As a user, I want EatPal to look like one product on every screen I own.
acceptanceCriteria: design/tokens.json holds colour (primary is the web carrot orange), the type scale and radii; a script generates src/index.css variables and ios/EatPal/EatPal/Utilities/AppTheme.swift, and CI fails if a generated file is stale
AppTheme.swift no longer uses Color.green; the Swift palette resolves to the same hex values as the web tokens in light and dark

Web and Swift agree on the type scale; families are recorded in the token file even where Swift uses the system font
userStories.notes: Review item X6.

userStories.title: Split the four core pages and bound the Swift load
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the core-loop pages small enough to test so that they stop being the riskiest files in the repo.
acceptanceCriteria: Pantry.tsx, Grocery.tsx, Recipes.tsx and Planner.tsx each drop below 500 lines by extracting a data-derivation hook and a dialog host; behaviour is pinned by the integration test from US-735 before and after
Each of the four pages gains at least one render test
ios/EatPal/EatPal/App/AppState.swift loadAllData applies the same windows and limits web uses (plan window, movement window, recipe and food limits)

userStories.notes: Review items X9, X12 (file size). The Swift half is loopVerifiable false.

userStories.title: Parity fixtures for units, aisles, scaling and shortfall
userStories.description: As the release owner, I want the numbers a user sees on iOS and web to come from the same rules so that the two clients cannot drift.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/fixtures gains unit-conversion-cases.json, aisle-classify-cases.json (from US-728), recipe-scaling-cases.json and shortfall-cases.json
Each fixture is asserted by a vitest under src/lib and an XCTest under ios/EatPal/EatPalTests, following SharedIngredientParseCasesTests
canonicalUnits.ts and UnitConverter.swift, recipeShortfall.ts and PantryCoverage.swift, and a new src/lib/recipeScaling.ts mirroring RecipeScaling.swift all pass their fixture
ios-ci.yml and ci.yml both run the fixture suites; a fixture change without both tests passing fails CI
userStories.notes: Review item X3. Extends kitchen-loop US-660.

userStories.title: Swift adopts the household planner model
userStories.description: As an iOS user, I want the App Store app to use the same meals, eaters, ledger and resolver as web so that my household's two devices agree.
acceptanceCriteria: Kitchen-loop US-682, US-683, US-684 are complete (resolver, ledger-backed cook, buy and pantry edit, resolver at import)
MealPlanView reads meals and plates, renders eaters including adults, and supports kind and recurrence from US-742
GroceryView reads aisle_section and walk order from the shared taxonomy and writes purchase movements at checkout
Tabs become Today, Week, Recipes, Grocery (List and Pantry segments), Kids per kitchen-loop US-685 to US-687, with the provenance thread
Onboarding branches on who are you planning for, matching web
Verified on a Mac with Xcode against a staging Supabase; never marked passing from this machine
userStories.notes: Review items X2, and the iOS halves of P2, G8, G28. Ships as release N+1; kitchen-loop US-689 retires the mirrors after MIN_SUPPORTED_IOS_BUILD passes it.
